topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: Bridging Primes and Patterns
target_audience: Undergraduate students with basic calculus knowledge

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Harmonic Series
lecture_lines: Consider the harmonic series sum 1/n.
When s=1, the series diverges.
Increasing s makes terms shrink faster.
animations: Display the harmonic series: 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 +... in #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Show partial sums S_N = sum_{n=1}^N 1/n using a moving bar chart.
Show the series diverges to infinity, with #FF4500 text indicating growth. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
lecture_lines: Define zeta(s) as the infinite sum.
Input complex numbers into the function.
Observe outputs on the complex plane.
Different s values map to unique points.
These points form elegant geometric structures.
animations: Write zeta(s) = sum_{n=1}^infty n^{-s} on screen in #00FFFF.
Animate s as a complex variable moving across the plane.
Display the complex plane with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] to show convergence/divergence.
Visualize the mapping from s to zeta(s) using a morphing transformation.
Show the resulting output points forming a smooth geometric pattern in #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Bridge: The Euler Product Formula
lecture_lines: The Euler product relates sum to primes.
Primes act as filters for integers.
This reveals hidden prime number structure.
It connects analysis to prime theory.
A beautiful bridge between different fields.
animations: Write zeta(s) = prod_{p} (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} in #FFFF00.
Animate the expansion of the product into the infinite sum.
Show prime numbers 2, 3, 5, 7,... appearing as key building blocks.
Use a color-coding (e.g., #00FF00 for primes) to show them as "filters" [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/filter.svg].
Show the equality bridging the two formulas in a balanced visual state [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg].

sections.title: The Mystery: Analytic Continuation & The Critical Strip
lecture_lines: We extend the function via continuation.
The critical strip holds chaotic behavior.
Zeros here define the Riemann Hypothesis.
It is like unfolding a map.
We search for these hidden zeros.
animations: Display the complex plane with sigma and t axes highlighted in #FFFFFF [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg].
Highlight the vertical strip from 0 to 1 with a light #333333 fill.
Animate the line at sigma = 1/2 in #FF0000.
Show dots representing zeros popping up along the critical line.
Highlight the zeros with a fading glow effect in #FFFF00 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion: Why it Matters
lecture_lines: Zeros reveal prime distribution patterns.
This connects primes to a symphony.
It remains a major open problem.
animations: Overlay the prime distribution graph with the zeta zeros.
Display the prime number theorem pi(x) ~ Li(x) in #00FF00.
Flash a large question mark over the Riemann Hypothesis to signify the open problem.
